notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0. result.json gives head 80b4f6e with uncommitted true and skill_hash 38af1e43dc9687295662406f956bc486af6604774a385309c75570733d642de5, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the current text. git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only the do: rule in SKILL.md (its last sentence, plus a message/1 Instead-of/write pair in its example) and the test-name paragraph of "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" in references/testing.md, which no macro-dsl rule covers.

Unchanged rules: macros.md and library-design.md are unchanged since 0397dec, so the seven macro and library rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, validation in the macro body outside quote does not; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden); `if not ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule; a one-line three-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; a format failure whose only change is parentheses on the two get calls is recorded as ok apart from locals_without_parens; String.to_atom on route text from source code is not counted under the atom rule.

Changed rule, graded against its current text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else. The sentence "A one-expression body too long for the head's line wants a block or a helper; a head that `mix format` wraps because of a long guard is fine as wrapped." is now "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line: when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`, so write a block or move part of the body into a helper. The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line." Those two sentences decide the wrapped-line verdicts. Violating runs out of four, per sentence. "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head": 0 of 4. "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 of 4. "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line.": 0 of 4 (every block clause is set apart, and every block holding one expression would wrap under do:, so no short clause went into a block). "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.": 0 of 4 (no function has blocks for more than half its clauses). "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line ... write a block or move part of the body into a helper.": 0 of 4 for function definitions. "The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line.": not exercised; no head in any of the four files is guard-wrapped. Any sentence: 0 of 4, so both tiers are clean. The with-skill sweep 2026-10-22-b had 2 of 5 (haiku-2 on a wrapped do: line, sonnet-1 on the clause-consistency sentence) and check-3 had 2 of 4 (both on the clause-consistency sentence).

Every do: body that mix format leaves on a line of its own, quoted: haiku-1 none; sonnet-1 none; sonnet-2 none; haiku-2 one, lines 64-65: `if not module_name?(handler),` / `do: fail(env, "expected a module name as handler, got: #{inspect(handler)}")`. That is an if, not a function head, so there is no guard and no long guard; haiku-2 wrote it already wrapped in its Write call (110 characters joined, which mix format would wrap the same way). It is graded outside the do: rule because every sentence of the rule speaks of function heads, clauses and guards and every example is a def, so haiku-2 stays clean. This is a judgement call: read with an if's condition line as "the head's line", the new sentence would make haiku-2 violated, and the count would be 1 of 4. The rule could say whether it covers keyword do: on if and unless.

Mixed-clause functions per run: all four write the segment matcher as four clauses, with two short do: clauses (the [], [] base case and the catch-all :error) and two recursive block clauses, each set apart by blank lines: haiku-1 bind/3 lines 104-114, haiku-2 match_segments/3 lines 103-113, sonnet-1 match_segments/3 lines 97-107, sonnet-2 match_segments/3 lines 107-117. haiku-2 also has module_name?/1 (lines 87-91) with one block clause and one do: clause. Each one-expression block body was rewritten as a do: line and run through Code.format_string!; every one wraps: haiku-1 151 and 107 characters, haiku-2 116 and 136 (plus module_name?/1 111, fail/2 121, generated match/1 107), sonnet-1 157 and 133, sonnet-2 141 and 117. The blocks are therefore needed, and two of four is not most, so the mixed form is clean everywhere, as in 2026-10-22-b and check-3.

Compile-time dependencies were checked with mix xref trace in one scratch Mix project per run. Each run's file was copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, so xref line numbers match the run file, with real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. haiku-1 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:call, 2}), sonnet-1 ({:routes, 0}) and sonnet-2 ({:match, 1}) report alias MyApp.PageHandler (runtime). haiku-2 never expands the handler and passes the alias into __define__/3, which runs in the router's module body, so xref reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile). That is the route both haiku runs took in 2026-10-22-b.

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project was loaded, then one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and another declaring get "/", "not a module" were compiled with Code.compile_string. All eight fail while the router compiles. haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 fail with ArgumentError from __define__/3, which get's quote calls; haiku-2 fails with CompileError from fail/2, which __define__/3 calls with __ENV__'s file and line. The messages omit the nofile:3: prefix.

Format: haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 pass mix format --check-formatted; they wrote get("/", MyApp.PageHandler) with parentheses. haiku-2 fails it only because lines 119-120 have get "/", MyApp.PageHandler without parentheses (result.json format_ok false). haiku-2 saw this failure in its last check and stopped there. All four compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors.

Reads: all four read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md before writing the file. haiku-1 and haiku-2 used one Read call per file; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md with Read and both references with one cat in a Bash call. This matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line.

Against 2026-10-22-b's skill runs: Keep quote blocks small is now clean on Sonnet (2-b sonnet-1 wrote the attribute directly in get's quote; all four runs here call __define__/3). The compile-time-dependency rule is still violated on Haiku, by haiku-2 only; haiku-1 now uses Macro.expand_literals. The do: rule went from violated on both tiers to clean on both. Three of four runs again write the one-line three-step pipeline in __before_compile__; sonnet-2 splits it over lines, as in 2-b.

Outside the rules: haiku-1's final reply is "/Users/suazithustra/tiny_router.ex", not the path it wrote, though the file is in the right place. Smoke test: all four return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", return :error for "/nope", and raise FunctionClauseError on match(123). haiku-1 and haiku-2 return atom param keys (%{id: "42"}) and sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 string keys (%{"id" => "42"}).
